title: Don't paste the AI, please
author: pjerem
relevanceReason: 命中 3 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Prefer another language? Don't pastethe AI, please. When someone asks you something, they want your answer. Not a wall of unedited ChatGPT output. A short reply from you beats a long one from a model, every time.

What's happening Someone asked you a real question. You popped it into a chatbot, copied the answer, and sent it back. It felt fast. It felt helpful. And it usually isn't. The person on the other side has the same tools you do. If they wanted the generic answer, they would have gotten it in four seconds. They asked you because they wanted your take on it... Your context, your taste, your judgement.
The world is filled with people that don't want to read or think about things, don't be one of them.

Try this instead Use the AI. Really, go for it. It's a great drafting partner. Just read what it gave you, then write your own take on it, don't just be the proxy between it and the answer. Pull out the bit that actually answers the question. Drop the rest. Three sentences from you is plenty. If a piece of the model's answer is genuinely useful, quote it and say why. I checked with Claude and this part lines up:" works great. If you don't have anything to add, it's okay to say so. "No strong opinion here" is a real, helpful reply.
Want to send this to someone? If someone just dropped a wall of model output in your DMs, Slack, or PR review, you can send them this link. No lecture required. Click to copy. They'll get the hint.

comments.author: disillusioned
comments.textRawHtml:
Heh. Just got done writing (by hand!) a Principles of AI Use document for my (ironically) AI enablement firm, the first of which is:

Write as yourself. You’re being paid for your expertise and insights. Communicate them directly to us. Copying and pasting Claude responses into Slack or an email directly shifts the burden of comprehension and understanding to everyone else, and worse, risks skipping that step for yourself. Even if you’re fundamentally using Claude to gather your thoughts or help you prepare a response, you need to be writing it yourself, in your own voice. Not having Claude ape your voice, or “make it sound less like AI”. You, directly. Doing this will further reinforce your own understanding of the state of things, the same way teaching someone is the best way to learn. As a guideline: for Slack and email comms, this should be near-universally written as you. For deliverables that are longer form and follow a template like proposals, roadmap/discovery work, etc., use of agents is expected but, see Principle #2. (Own the Output.)
comments.textZhHtml:
呵呵。刚刚为我的（讽刺的是）人工智能支持公司写了（手写！）人工智能使用原则文档，其中第一个是：

以你自己的方式编写。您的报酬是基于您的专业知识和见解。直接与我们沟通。将 Claude 的回复复制并粘贴到 Slack 或电子邮件中，会直接将理解和理解的负担转移给其他人，更糟糕的是，您可能会跳过这一步。即使你从根本上使用克劳德来收集你的想法或帮助你准备回应，你也需要自己用自己的声音来写。不要让克劳德模仿你的声音，或者“让它听起来不像人工智能”。你，直接。这样做将进一步加强你自己对事物状态的理解，就像教别人是最好的学习方式一样。作为指导：对于 Slack 和电子邮件通信，这应该几乎是按照您的方式编写的。对于较长形式并遵循提案、路线图/发现工作等模板的可交付成果，预计使用代理，但请参阅原则#2。 （拥有输出。）

children.author: mscbuck
children.textRawHtml: Just want to say, "Copying and pasting Claude responses into Slack or an email directly shifts the burden of comprehension and understanding to everyone else" is something that I don't think I really internalized until you wrote it in that way. Which I think is evidence of what you are talking about.
children.textZhHtml: 只是想说，“将 Claude 的回复复制并粘贴到 Slack 或电子邮件中，直接将理解和理解的负担转移给其他人”，在你以这种方式写之前，我认为我并没有真正内化。我认为这就是你所说的证据。

children.author: blensor
children.textRawHtml:
Tangentially I also hate if someone answers with a voice message.

I can understand that there are situations where you just can't type out the answer and those exceptions are of course fine, but if you post a voice message or god forbid a video message in a group chat you are forcing everyone to take the time and sit through it.
children.textZhHtml:
顺便说一句，我也讨厌有人用语音消息回答。

我可以理解，在某些情况下，你就是无法输入答案，这些例外当然没问题，但如果你在群聊中发布语音消息或上帝禁止在群聊中发送视频消息，你就会迫使每个人花时间坐下来完成它。

children.author: biztos
children.textRawHtml:
The WhatsApp voice message is very common in Spain. I always find it jarring when I'm there, mostly because I'm not used to it, but also because it seems to defeat the purpose of the messaging app: I can't listen to your voice message on the bus, for instance.

It's so normalized there that I wonder whether this is a particularly Spanish habit. Maybe there are a bunch of countries where people routinely leave each other voice recordings on WhatsApp/Messenger/etc, and I just haven't been to them yet.
children.textZhHtml:
WhatsApp 语音消息在西班牙非常常见。当我在那里时，我总是觉得很不舒服，主要是因为我不习惯，但也因为它似乎违背了消息应用程序的目的：例如，我无法在公交车上听你的语音消息。

那里太正常化了，我想知道这是否是一个特别的西班牙习惯。 也许有很多国家/地区的人们经常在 WhatsApp/Messenger/等上留下彼此的录音，而我只是还没有去过这些国家。

children.author: whstl
children.textRawHtml: I used to answer this with "I'm not listening to that, not even my parents send me voice messages" but it was called uncivil by some people, so now I just say "I can't listen to that right now" and never listen, eventually ppl send a text message.
children.textZhHtml: 我以前的回答是“我不听，连我父母都不给我发语音消息”，但被一些人认为不文明，所以现在我只是说“我现在不能听”然后就不听了，最后大家发短信了。

children.author: strenholme
children.textRawHtml: The way I handle those, especially with the people who leave me 8 minute long voice notes, is to have WhatsApp transcribe the voice note for me.  Or, if that’s not possible, either ignore the voice note or listen to it at 2x speed.
children.textZhHtml: 我处理这些问题的方式，尤其是那些给我留下 8 分钟长语音留言的人，是让 WhatsApp 为我转录语音留言。  或者，如果不可能，请忽略语音注释或以 2 倍速收听。

children.author: blensor
children.textRawHtml: I can't understand why whatsapp does not provide tgat out of the box. Telegram has it on the paid plan, which is nit ideal but at least somewhat out of the box solution.
children.textZhHtml: 我不明白为什么 Whatsapp 不提供开箱即用的 tgat。 Telegram 将其纳入付费计划，这并不理想，但至少在某种程度上是开箱即用的解决方案。

children.author: biztos
children.textRawHtml: I was surprised WhatsApp didn't give me a "transcribe" button (as recently as yesterday).  Seems like it'd be pretty easy to implement that.
children.textZhHtml: 我很惊讶 WhatsApp 没有给我一个“转录”按钮（就在昨天）。  看起来实现起来很容易。

children.author: strenholme
children.textRawHtml: I don’t have a transcribe button in the Windows app, but my Android phone has a transcribe button.
children.textZhHtml: 我的 Windows 应用程序中没有转录按钮，但我的 Android 手机有转录按钮。

children.author: kspacewalk2
children.textRawHtml: Maybe it's a cultural thing in the Spanish speaking world? Had the same experience in Colombia.
children.textZhHtml: 也许这是西班牙语世界的一种文化？在哥伦比亚也有同样的经历。

children.author: winstonp
children.textRawHtml: It's a habit in specific countries, China is one in my experience.
children.textZhHtml: 这是特定国家的一种习惯，根据我的经验，中国就是其中之一。

children.author: prepend
children.textRawHtml:
It’s funny to me how I judge some cultural aspects as being worse. Of course it’s my own cultural bias, but I think the following things are “bad” for cultures to do:

1) long voice memos over succinctly typed notes

2) not forming lines/queues and just mobbing the train/shop/etc

3) habitually late or not on time
children.textZhHtml:
我认为某些文化方面更糟糕，这对我来说很有趣。当然，这是我自己的文化偏见，但我认为以下事情对文化来说是“不好的”：

1）长语音备忘录而不是简洁打字的笔记

2）不排队/排队，只是围攻火车/商店/等

3）习惯性迟到或不准时

children.author: dummydummy1234
children.textRawHtml: Was just in south America, everyone uses it.
children.textZhHtml: 就在南美洲，每个人都使用它。

children.author: tayo42
children.textRawHtml: Are the messages in Spanish or English?
children.textZhHtml: 这些消息是西班牙语还是英语？

children.author: wreath
children.textRawHtml: Same here. I sometimes dont feel like typing but I use voice dictation, that should be the first option in a text convo imo.
children.textZhHtml: 这里也一样。我有时不想打字，但我使用语音听写，在我看来，这应该是文本对话中的第一个选项。

children.author: therealdrag0
children.textRawHtml: I use dictation a lot and god it’s so bad. I have to correct something every single time.
children.textZhHtml: 我经常使用听写，天哪，这太糟糕了。我每次都必须纠正一些东西。

children.author: fn-mote
children.textRawHtml:
Fortunately, if they send it as a text message or voicemail, I get automatic transcription.

Too bad that’s not more universal.
children.textZhHtml:
幸运的是，如果他们以短信或语音邮件的形式发送，我会得到自动转录。

太糟糕了，这并不更通用。

children.author: mapontosevenths
children.textRawHtml:
Literacy is dying. I suspect that's part of the reason some people hate AI.

To the semi-literate a few paragraphs of text represent a significant investment of their time.
children.textZhHtml:
读写能力正在消亡。我怀疑这就是一些人讨厌人工智能的部分原因。

对于半文盲的人来说，几段文字代表了他们的大量时间投入。

children.author: oldmanhorton
children.textRawHtml: I think this is a pretty unfair takeaway when AI generated text is often so wordy, flowery, and full of jargon and abstract nouns. People are never going to read East of Eden or academic dissertations as quickly as direct, simple language either
children.textZhHtml: 我认为这是一个相当不公平的结论，因为人工智能生成的文本通常非常罗嗦、华丽，并且充满了行话和抽象名词。人们永远不会像直接、简单的语言那样快速地阅读《伊甸园之东》或学术论文
